ELS-1099.text: Dear <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Zia</custom> we’ve already saw email from Adarsh, it’s clearly, so we’re testing follow their recommend. Thank you for your support.

ELS-1099.author: Joo
ELS-1099.text:
Hi <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Zia</custom>  cc <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-1">@Joseph</custom> <custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-2">@Harry</custom> 

We are currently in the process of integration testing and bug fixing while pushing data to Google.

* Tested & passed:

‌       Room (RoomTransformService) — ✅ pass  
       Rate Plan (RatePlanTransformService) — ✅ pass  
       Rate (RateTransformService) — ✅ pass  
       Inventory (InventoryTransformService) — ✅ pass  
       Promotion (PromotionTransformService) — ✅ pass

‌       Availability (AvailabilityTransformService) — ✅ pass

* Test progress:  
  Promotion Manual (RateModificationsTransformService)  
  Stop Sell / Cut-off (CutOffStopSellPushService)  
  Re-test all flow
* Landing page:

‌      Received email from Google and started testing  
      Successfully able to redirect back to OMH  
      However, we are encountering an issue where the data returned from Google does not match the original format, specifically the rate plan sequence       (rateplan_seq)  
     This mismatch is causing inconsistencies in the mapping process  
     Currently working on fixing this and testing additional cases

* Issues identified and resolved:

Google rejected past-date data (Inventory / Availability / Rate) → added filtering logic  
Retry mechanism became inactive after merge → fixed

* Ongoing work:

Re-run E2E after fixes  
Backfill test coverage  
Continue validating additional landing page cases

* Blocker:

NTH_NIGHT_FREE (manual promotion) still has no clear mapping approach

We will continue to provide updates as progress is made.

Thanks!

ELS-1099.author: Zia
ELS-1099.text:
<custom data-type="mention" data-id="id-0">@Joo</custom> Thanks for the update.

On the NTH_NIGHT_FREE blocker - I left a comment earlier today at 11:09am. The gist: moving to a rate plan may not actually rule out `<FreeNights>` (it can be scoped to a specific PackageID and layered on top of the rate plan), so I asked the team to validate whether that composition holds against the schema. Could you check that comment first and share what you find? Thanks!
